source.name: sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo
    @OrderID INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/address)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(500)') AS ShippingAddress,
        m.MetadataXml.value('(/order/shipping/method)[1]', 'NVARCHAR(100)') AS ShippingMethod,
        m.MetadataXml.query('/order/items') AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = @OrderID;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetOrderShippingInfo(
    p_OrderID INTEGER
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderID INTEGER,
    ShippingAddress VARCHAR(500),
    ShippingMethod VARCHAR(100),
    ItemsXml XML
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        o.OrderID,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/address/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(500) AS ShippingAddress,
        (xpath('/order/shipping/method/text()', m.MetadataXml))[1]::TEXT::VARCHAR(100) AS ShippingMethod,
        (xpath('/order/items', m.MetadataXml))[1]::XML AS ItemsXml
    FROM dbo.Orders o
    INNER JOIN dbo.OrderMetadata m ON o.OrderID = m.OrderID
    WHERE o.OrderID = p_OrderID;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The MetadataXml column in OrderMetadata table is of type XML in PostgreSQL
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL database
SQL Server's .value() method is converted to xpath() function with array indexing
SQL Server's .query() method is converted to xpath() function returning XML
NVARCHAR is mapped to VARCHAR in PostgreSQL (UTF-8 encoding is default)
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default in functions)

reviewFlags.reason: XPath syntax and behavior differs between SQL Server and PostgreSQL. SQL Server's .value() method with XPath may handle namespaces, default values, and null handling differently than PostgreSQL's xpath() function. Test with actual XML data to ensure correct extraction.

SQL Server's .query() method returns XML fragments differently than PostgreSQL's xpath(). The xpath() function returns an array of XML nodes. Verify that the returned XML structure matches the expected format, especially for complex nested elements.
Verify that the MetadataXml column in OrderMetadata table is actually of type XML in PostgreSQL. If it's stored as TEXT, additional casting may be required.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's XQuery methods (.value(), .query()) have different syntax and semantics compared to PostgreSQL's xpath() function. PostgreSQL xpath() returns an array of XML nodes, requiring array indexing [1] to get the first match. Text extraction requires explicit ::TEXT casting.

SQL Server stored procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL requires explicit RETURNS TABLE definition and RETURN QUERY statement. Calling code must be updated to SELECT FROM the function instead of EXEC.

If XPath expressions don't match any nodes, PostgreSQL xpath() returns an empty array. Accessing [1] on an empty array returns NULL. SQL Server's .value() may have different NULL handling behavior depending on the XPath expression.
SQL Server NVARCHAR uses UCS-2/UTF-16 encoding. PostgreSQL VARCHAR uses UTF-8 by default. This should be functionally equivalent for most use cases but may affect byte length calculations.
